papers.title: Robustness of Magic and the Directed Geometry of State Conversion
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and show that RoM is exactly represented as the distance to the free-state set. We then extend this geometry to state conversion by defining the directed conversion deficiency $C_{\mathcal F}$ as the distance between a target state and the set of states freely reachable from a given input state. The quantity $C_{\mathcal F}$ characterizes free convertibility and is related to the minimum stabilizer quasiprobability weight required to represent the conversion residual through the relation $1+2C_{\mathcal F}$. It also contains the conventional magic state resource lower bounds based on RoM and can detect stronger conversion obstructions. For single-qubit systems, we analytically construct a continuous family of mixed states with identical RoM but asymmetric convertibility.

papers.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
papers.abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.

papers.title: An odd version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra and the odd Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We study an ``odd'' version of the Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra that is obtained by replacing free Lie algebras in even generators by free graded Lie algebras in odd generators in the classical definition. These odd variants are related to the ``odd'' Kontsevich graph complex in the same way as the classical Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller group is related to the even Kontsevich graph complex. We show an odd analog of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, namely that the odd Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra is isomorphic to a free graded Lie algebra in one odd generator of weight 3. Thus we in particular compute the odd graph cohomology in the bottom cohomological degree, showing that it is mostly zero.

papers.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

papers.title: Non-Clifford quantum cellular automata from invertible topological quantum field theories
papers.abstract: Quantum cellular automata (QCAs) describe locality-preserving quantum dynamics and link quantum information, many-body physics, and topological quantum field theory (TQFT). Constructing a QCA from a TQFT, however, remains challenging: although a topological action yields a Hamiltonian with commuting terms that realizes the desired ground state, it does not by itself specify an automorphism of the full operator algebra. We develop a unified algebraic construction that extends such Hamiltonians to complete separator-flipper algebras on the full tensor-product Hilbert space, thereby defining the corresponding QCAs microscopically. In 3 spatial dimensions, our framework unifies all previously known QCA constructions associated with the $\mathbb{Z}_8\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup of the Witt group, including the $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ QCAs. The same algebraic structure yields new infinite families of generalized $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ non-Clifford QCAs in spatial dimensions $d=4k-1$. We also reformulate the 4-dimensional $w_2w_3$ QCA and use it to construct QCAs from TQFTs associated with arbitrary products of Stiefel--Whitney classes. For example, we explicitly construct two infinite families: $w_2^nw_3^m$ QCAs in dimension $d=2n+3m-1$ and $w_2w_{4k-1}$ QCAs in dimension $d=4k$. For the 5-dimensional $w_3^2$ and $w_2^3$ QCAs, our construction gives finite-depth quantum circuits, consistent with the cobordism classification. More generally, we show that our construction yields a finite-depth quantum circuit whenever the corresponding Stiefel-Whitney number vanishes on every closed oriented manifold. Overall, these results convert invertible TQFTs into microscopic QCAs, provide higher-dimensional constructions beyond the Clifford setting, and open a systematic route to characterizing their stable structures and boundary anomalies.

papers.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern-Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux-charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov-Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel-Watts theory.

papers.title: Restricted conformal blocks and the braiding on Zhu algebra modules
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra (VOA), not necessarily rational or $C_2$-cofinite, such that the category $\mathcal C_1(V)$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is semisimple and contains the generalized Verma modules associated to finite-dimensional modules over the Zhu algebra $A(V)$. Such VOAs include affine VOAs at admissible and generic levels. We prove that the bottom degree of Huang-Lepowsky's $P(w)$-tensor product module $M^1\boxtimes_{P(w)}M^2$ is isomorphic to the left $A(V)$-module $M^1\odot_{w,0}M^2$ arising from the restricted conformal blocks on $(\P^1,\infty,w,0)$. By shifting the marked points and using the parallel transport of the restricted conformal blocks, we construct an explicit braiding isomorphism on the category of finite-dimensional $A(V)$-modules, which is the restriction of the braiding isomorphism of Huang-Lepowsky-Zhang to the bottom degrees. For the affine VOA $L_k(\mathfrak g)$ at a positive integral level, it is given by the Casimir tensor of $\mathfrak g$ on certain quotients of tensor products of finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules, and at generic levels it recovers Drinfeld's commutativity isomorphism.

papers.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles
papers.abstract: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension. In a role of a fibre we either take a left $H$-comodule algebra $F$, or more generally an internal $F$-coring $N$ in the monoidal category of left $H$-comodules. Cotensor products combining these data is used to obtain an ordinary coring representing the total space of an associated bundle. If the fiber coring $N$ is equipped with a choice of an $H$-coinvariant grouplike element, then we exhibit a canonical morphisms of corings from the $H$-coinvariant coring of $M$ to the associated bundle coring which is viewed as a dual to the projection of an associated bundle.

papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\CC$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

papers.title: Finite Composites of the Fibonacci Category with Pointed Fusion Categories
papers.abstract: We classify finite composites of the positive Fibonacci category with arbitrary pointed fusion categories, retaining the entire source functor and making no unitarity assumption on the target. Formal codegrees, dimension fields, and algebraic integrality exclude all dihedral Fibonacci rings $R_n$ with $n\ge4$ from categorification. Together with an independent graphical uniqueness argument, this gives the finite two-Fibonacci classification. For several marked Fibonacci generators, a geometric height-and-polygon argument identifies the based ring with a standard-basis Coxeter--Hecke ring. Transitive conjugation by the pointed image forces the noncommutation graph to be empty or a perfect matching. We then obtain a crossed-product classification in terms of a quotient group, a stabilizer, labelled Fibonacci or rank-six $\TT$ blocks, and compatible cocycle and categorical action data. This includes the Fibonacci--$\Z/3\Z$ composite problem without target unitarity. We also establish the corresponding forms and marked descent statements over characteristic-zero fields admitting the chosen Fibonacci-type input.

papers.title: Monopole-Fermion Scattering from Twisted Conformal Boundary States
papers.abstract: We derive monopole-fermion scattering correlators from conformal boundary states in twisted sectors. The key ingredient is that symmetry-preserving boundary conditions contain sectors twisted by topological symmetry lines. Their overlaps determine correlators of operators attached to these lines, including the outgoing excitations required by charge conservation in the Callan-Rubakov effect. We construct the twisted boundary states of $N$ free Dirac fermions with $U(1)^N$-preserving boundary conditions, extending the familiar description in terms of charge lattices to shifted lattices describing twisted sectors. Using cluster decomposition and open-closed duality, we determine their coefficients and fix their normalization relative to the untwisted boundary state. We find that the Callan-Rubakov boundary condition yields a two-point function between an incoming fermion and an outgoing defect operator with a coefficient of unit modulus, even when the corresponding correlators of ordinary local fermions vanish. Finally, we relate these correlators to four-dimensional partial-wave scattering using gauge-covariant asymptotic states. We identify the missing $s$-wave contribution to the unitarity relation and argue that the twisted channel supplies it with precisely the required normalization.

papers.title: Schopieray's Galois-modular extension conjecture
papers.abstract: Plavnik, Schopieray, Yu, and Zhang have drawn attention to those (automatically premodular) fusion subcategories of modular fusion categories which are submodules for the Galois action on the ambient category. In particular, they showed that a subcategory is a Galois submodule if and only if its centralizer is integral. In the other direction, Schopieray has conjectured that every premodular fusion category can be embedded as a Galois-closed subcategory of a modular category; Schopieray calls such an embedding a \emph{Galois-modular extension}. We prove Schopieray's conjecture for pseudounitary categories; in the nonpseudounitary case, we prove that every braided fusion category admits a "Galois nondegenerate extension" but we do not know it to be modular. Along the way we record some general comments about the minimal nondegenerate extension problem for braided fusion categories.
